attribution.note: Marcus wrote and endorsed the conclusion being assessed; it is not one of the surrounding quotations from others.

semantics.note: In context, the statement firmly rejects the prospect of perfectly reliable LLM chatbots within a year. The normalization preserves that outcome and approximate horizon; there is no explicit antecedent.

contract.note: The contract substitutes finite benchmark results for perfect chatbot reliability. Zero observed errors on one test would not establish perfection, while errors among listed models do not establish that no qualifying chatbot existed. This proxy changes the speaker's scope and can determine the grade.

evidence.note: The dated snapshot fits the contract's approximate February window and reports nonzero hallucination rates for every listed model. It supports imperfection of those models on summarization, but does not establish coverage of all available chatbots or RAG systems.

output.rationale: The deadline has passed. The leaderboard supports continued hallucinations in tested models, with the best listed rate at 0.7%. But the packet contains only one summarization benchmark, not sufficient coverage of available chatbot and RAG systems to settle the universal forecast. Treating it as conclusive would depend on the contract's unsupported proxy. No material counterevidence was supplied.
